clue.text: Biblical beauty in Paris is that woman?

parts.note: est is French for 'is', the language of Paris
her refers to that woman

explanation.surface: Asks whether some beautiful woman in Paris is the biblical heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: EST is the French for 'is'; HER is 'that woman'.
explanation.definitionFit: Esther was the beautiful Jewish queen of Persia in the Old Testament book named after her.

clue.text: Person by turns to meet with deep disappointment

indicators.note: the pieces are joined end to end, one meeting the next

parts.note: a bod is informal British for a person

indicators.note: turns tells us the word by is flipped round

parts.note: a deep voice is a low one

explanation.surface: Someone is taking turns to face a crushing letdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person' is British slang here, a bod; 'deep' is the sense of a low voice or note.
explanation.definitionFit: A body blow is figuratively a severe setback, a heavy disappointment that knocks one back.

clue.text: Get out boxes ready with cold battered chicken

indicators.note: boxes means the first word encloses the other letters

parts.note: scat is a command meaning go away, get out

indicators.note: battered means the letters are knocked about into a new order

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A kitchen instruction: take out boxes and prepare chicken battered with something cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battered chicken' reads like a recipe, but 'chicken' is the definition, slang for a coward; 'battered' is the mixing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken is slang for a coward, as is a scaredy-cat.

clue.text: Confined an enormous bird inside small bottle

indicators.note: inside places the bird within the bottle's letters

parts.note: a phial is a small glass bottle
an gives the article A
the roc is a giant mythical bird

explanation.surface: A huge bird has been squeezed into a little bottle, like a ship in a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: The roc is the giant bird of the Arabian Nights; 'Confined' is used in its sense of narrow-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: Parochial means narrow in outlook, limited to a small local area.

clue.text: Ultimately flood may soak the ditch

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Eventually a flood might saturate the ditch.
explanation.definitionFit: A dyke can be a drainage channel or trench as well as an embankment.

clue.text: Surrounded by 500 in a film

indicators.note: in places the Roman numeral within the other letters

parts.note: a mist is a thin film or haze
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Someone is surrounded by five hundred people in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' looks like a movie but is a thin layer, a MIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Amidst is a preposition meaning in the middle of, encircled by.

clue.text: Female gave evil look and came out

parts.note: to lower (or lour) is to scowl or frown darkly

explanation.surface: A woman glared menacingly and then emerged.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that has flowered has bloomed, its blossoms having opened.

clue.text: Job was so useless in the end — about to stop work

indicators.note: in the end picks only the final letter of useless
to stop means the short word plugs the middle of the other

parts.note: toil is hard work
CA (circa) means about

explanation.surface: A job was hopeless in the end, so someone is about to down tools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Job' is not employment but the biblical Job, famed for patience. S ends 'useless'; CA plugs TOIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Job endured his trials patiently and uncomplainingly, which is to be stoic in character.

clue.text: Luxurious boozer

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both richly opulent and, as slang, a habitual drunkard.

clue.text: Infant tiny, uncovered? That's dreadful

indicators.note: uncovered strips the outer letters from the combined words

parts.note: a baby is an infant
small means tiny

explanation.surface: Seeing a tiny baby left without blankets is shocking.
explanation.walkthrough: BABYSMALL loses its covering letters, B and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Abysmal means extremely bad, appallingly poor in quality.

clue.text: Angry nurses battle over trickster's command

indicators.note: nurses means holds within, as one nurses a baby

parts.note: het, as in het up, means heated or angry
Ypres was a series of First World War battles in Belgium
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Furious nurses fight over something.
explanation.walkthrough: HET holds YPRES, then O for over, a set of six balls in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjuror says it when a trick is completed, producing something as if by magic.

clue.text: Once enough to keep daughter and bequeath an income

indicators.note: to keep means the outer word holds the letter inside

parts.note: enow is an archaic word for enough, once used

explanation.surface: Once there was enough to support a daughter and leave her an inheritance.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to give a permanent fund or income to a person or institution.

clue.text: Food shop back next to King's Cross

indicators.note: next to sets the two pieces side by side

parts.note: R (Rex) is the abbreviation for king; the 's reads as 'is'

indicators.note: back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a food shop

explanation.surface: A food shop at the rear, beside King's Cross station in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King's Cross' looks like the London station; the definition is just 'Cross', meaning annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross means angry, and riled means annoyed or irritated.

clue.text: Trousers too long for fashionable person?

indicators.note: too long means the word has one letter too many, so its last is cut

parts.note: hipsters are trousers that sit on the hips

explanation.surface: Are these trousers too long for a trendy type?
explanation.definitionFit: A hipster is someone who follows the latest trends ahead of the mainstream.

clue.text: Boring President forced to tour America

indicators.note: to tour means the rearranged letters go round the other
forced means the letters are wrenched into a new order

explanation.surface: A dull president has been made to go on a tour of the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian means dull and uninspired, lacking imagination.

clue.text: Two articles by retired staff about Brussels institution

parts.note: A and THE are the indefinite and definite articles

indicators.note: about means the reversed word goes round the other
retired means drawn back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to man is to staff
the EU is headquartered in Brussels

explanation.surface: Some newspaper articles about Brussels by former staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' tells you to read the word for staff backwards; Brussels stands for the European Union it hosts.
explanation.definitionFit: An Athenaeum is a learned society or club, such as the London club of that name.

clue.text: House the boss here temporarily, as narc oddly went berserk

definitions.note: Sir Stephen House was acting Metropolitan Police Commissioner in 2022

indicators.note: berserk means wildly out of control, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A drugs officer behaved strangely and ran amok.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' is part of the fodder, not a signal to take odd letters. House was the stand-in head of the Met after Cressida Dick resigned.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the London headquarters of the Metropolitan Police, where its acting chief was based.

clue.text: Something obnoxious exists to split subtle difference

indicators.note: to split means the short word goes into the middle of the other

parts.note: a nuance is a subtle distinction
is means exists

explanation.surface: Something unpleasant exists to divide a fine distinction.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuisance is an annoying or offensive thing or person.

clue.text: English align converts with John

indicators.note: converts means the letters change into another form

parts.note: john and can are both slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: English people who convert line up with someone called John.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' is not a person but slang for a lavatory, and so is CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglican describes the Church of England, the English established church.

clue.text: Guest in Vietnam's capital is there occasionally

indicators.note: capital means the first, capital letter of the word
occasionally picks every other letter

explanation.surface: A guest in Hanoi sometimes visits.
explanation.definitionFit: An invitee is someone who has been invited, a guest.

clue.text: One wrecking vehicle young chap's driven up

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: driven up in a down clue means the word reads upwards, reversed

parts.note: a lad is a young chap; the 's reads as 'has'

explanation.surface: A young man has driven a vehicle into something and wrecked it.
explanation.definitionFit: A vandal is a person who wilfully destroys or damages property.

clue.text: This was taken from Samson and Lot

definitions.meaning: the Philistines put out Samson's eyes, taking his vision
a ... of something means a lot, as in a ... better

explanation.walkthrough: 'Samson and Lot' suggests two Old Testament figures; Lot is just a quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the power of seeing and, informally, a great deal.

clue.text: Banknote left in emptied tray

indicators.note: in means the word goes inside the remaining letters
emptied keeps only the outer letters of tray

parts.note: went means left, departed

explanation.surface: A banknote was left in a tray that had been cleared.
explanation.definitionFit: A twenty is a twenty-pound or twenty-dollar bill.

clue.text: Group using rhymes in Petrarchan sonnet

definitions.meaning: the octave of a Petrarchan sonnet rhymes ... ...

explanation.definitionFit: It names the Swedish band and the rhyme pattern of each quatrain in an Italian sonnet's octave.

clue.text: Virgin martyr gets on train finally coming in

indicators.note: coming in means the letter enters the other word

parts.note: ages means gets on, grows older

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of train

explanation.surface: A saint boards a train at the last moment.
explanation.definitionFit: St Agnes of Rome was a young virgin killed for her faith.

clue.text: Female heading to destination: Slough

parts.note: she is a female

indicators.note: heading to picks the first letter of destination

explanation.surface: A woman sets off for her destination, the town of Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a town west of London, but here it is a verb, to cast off skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake sloughs or sheds its skin, casting it off.

clue.text: Purple, gold, black, and one seen in green pants!

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold
B is the pencil abbreviation for black

indicators.note: seen in means the numeral sits inside the other letters
pants is slang for rubbish, signalling a poor arrangement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A clash of colours on someone wearing green trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' is not trousers but British slang for rubbish, so GREEN is rearranged into ERGNE, which takes I.
explanation.definitionFit: Aubergine is a dark purple colour, named after the vegetable's skin.

clue.text: Similar drinks going together with classy wine made here

parts.note: cha and tea are both words for the same drink
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: Similar drinks go well with a fine wine.
explanation.walkthrough: CHA is British slang for tea, so the two similar drinks are CHA and TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: A French wine estate with its own vineyard and buildings, where wine is produced.

clue.text: Very determined Armada man took ships

indicators.note: ships means carries, so the words carry the answer within them

explanation.surface: A determined man from the Spanish Armada seized vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant means unshakeably resolved, refusing to change one's mind.
